specs.value: Engineering Plate: The Engineering Plate is compatible with the full range of Bambu Lab filaments. Simply apply a thin layer of glue before printing. Cool Plate SuperTack: This plate is designed only for printing PLA and PETG. Using any other materials may damage the surface coating.
specs.source_title: Introduction to Bambu Lab Build Plates | Bambu Lab Wiki
specs.locator: Build Plate Types › Engineering Plate tab › Features › Compatible with All Filaments; Build Plate Types › Cool Plate SuperTack tab › paragraph 4 (⚠️ Note)
specs.quote: The Engineering Plate is compatible with the full range of Bambu Lab filaments. Simply apply a thin layer of glue before printing. … This plate is designed only for printing PLA and PETG.
specs.note: The two plates every Combo Type contains, each sentence verbatim under its wiki tab name (the store page's "Which Build Plate Is Right for You?" table gives the same two sentences as the Filament Precautions of these plates). The Cool Plate SuperTack sentence continues "Using any other materials may damage the surface coating." The store page adds for the SuperTack "Do NOT print with TPU filament, as it will damage the build plate." and does not recommend Bambu PLA Silk on it. The Textured PEI Plate (3-plate option only) is the option-scoped row below.
specs.conflict: The store page's product-scope compat.statement ("PEI enables printing not only with common materials such as PLA, TPU, PETG, but also with materials that require high temperatures like ABS and Nylon.") describes only the Textured PEI Plate, which the 2-plate Combo Type does not contain; it is kept as the 3-plate option row.

relations.locator: Build Plate › Build Plate Dimensions table (Dimensions | Compatible Models) › row 3
relations.quote: 256*256 mm | X2D / P2S / P1 Series / X1 Series / A1
relations.note: The store page sells the combo with the Printer Model option "X1/P1/A1 Series" (the deterministic layer already writes this relation from the option value); the wiki row is the size evidence. The wiki's Important Notice: the 256×256 mm Textured PEI Plate and Cool Plate SuperTack come in two generations (first generation for A1 and X1/P1, second generation for P2S/X2D; P2S/X2D can physically use first-generation plates without automatic plate recognition). The store page does not say which generation each option ships; its own note on the X2D/P2S variants asks to disable Build Plate Position Detection when printing with the Cool Plate SuperTack.

notes: A bundle of two or three different plates: the registry has no per-component scope, so facts that differ between the plates (material, thickness, surface, each plate's packaging size and weight, its own filament list and bed temperatures) stay as the deterministic per-plate x.* rows and description blocks, and only facts true for every plate of a scope are curated here.

Not curated: part.max_temperature for the 3-plate Combo Type (180 ℃ Textured PEI vs 120 ℃ for the other two); printing.supported_filament / unsupported_filament (they differ per plate; the compat.statement rows carry each plate's statement); a "requires glue" relation (only the Engineering Plate needs glue, and both Combo Types include a glue stick).

No in-the-box list is published; the Combo Type option names ("Cool Plate + Engineering (with Glue Stick)", "... + Texture PEl") are the only statement of contents, so in_the_box stays empty and package.contents is neither curated nor declared not_published.
package.* of the combo itself is not published, but each plate's own packaging is, so package.* is not declared not_published.
